summary: Configured a single failover gateway on node3's private network so node3 can reach node4 across the router pair (node1/node2), preferring node1 while healthy, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart and recovery protocol on all four nodes.
actions_performed: Empirically identified segment membership via temporary IP assignment and ping tests
Configured VyOS VRRP groups SEG-A and SEG-B on node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100), committed and saved
Configured static eth1 IPs and a single gateway route to the peer subnet on node3 and node4
Disrupted node1 (took eth1 and eth2 link down) to exercise failover, observed node2 become VRRP MASTER within seconds, confirmed near-uninterrupted ping from node3 to node4
Restored node1 link, confirmed VRRP preemption back to MASTER on node1

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially via native reboot, polling each until reachable, confirming changed boot id, and reverifying VRRP state and end-to-end connectivity after each restart

evidence.requirement: node3 has a single gateway to reach node4 preferring node1
evidence.summary: VRRP groups configured with node1 priority 200 as MASTER; node3 route points at VIP gateway; ping node3 to node4 succeeds

evidence.requirement: Gateway stays available when node1 is down
evidence.summary: node1 LAN interfaces taken down; node2 became VRRP MASTER within seconds; background ping showed only brief gap during failover

evidence.requirement: Gateway prefers node1 once healthy again
evidence.summary: node1 interfaces restored and preempted back to MASTER; connectivity fully healthy again
Boot id changed after reboot; VRRP MASTER role recovered on both segments
Boot id changed after reboot; rejoined as VRRP BACKUP on both segments
Boot id changed after reboot; static route to node4 persisted; ping succeeded
Boot id changed after reboot; static route to node3 persisted; ping from node3 succeeded confirming full recovery
